artists.biography:
The Bluetones were an English indie rock band, formed in Hounslow, Greater London, in 1993. The band's members were Mark Morriss on vocals, Adam Devlin on guitar, Scott Morriss on bass guitar, and Eds Chesters on drums. A fifth member, Richard Payne, came on board between 1998 and 2002. The band was originally named "The Bottlegarden".

The Bluetones' commercial success waned after the fall of the Britpop movement, yet they continued to tour and release new records and were therefore often labelled as "Britpop survivors".

The band's final album A New Athens was released on 31 May 2010.

The band split on 1 October 2011 following a farewell tour which ended with a concert in Osaka, Japan.

perplexity.description:
The Singles" is a compilation album by English rock band The Bluetones, originally released in 2002. The album gathers the band's most notable singles from their active years between 1995 and 2002, showcasing their signature blend of Britpop and alternative rock. Known for their melodic guitar-driven sound, catchy hooks, and introspective lyrics, The Bluetones deliver a collection that highlights their consistent songwriting and chart success during the Britpop era. Tracks such as "Slight Return," "Bluetonic," and "Marblehead Johnson" exemplify their knack for combining jangly guitar riffs with wistful, relatable themes.

As a career retrospective, "The Singles" serves as a definitive summary of The Bluetones' impact on the British rock scene, capturing their run of hit singles and their evolution over the late 1990s and early 2000s. The album was released on Superior Quality Recordings and later reissued by Demon Records, but its original 2002 release remains a key entry in the band's discography. While it did not achieve the same level of commercial success as some of their contemporaries, "The Singles" was well-received by fans and critics for its cohesive selection and enduring appeal, solidifying The Bluetones' reputation as one of the more enduring acts of the Britpop movement.
